as_told.title: Mentor in Princeton PEAR random event generator experiments

plain: At a Princeton lab that studied odd mental effects, known as PEAR, researchers ran machines called random event generators, which spit out random numbers, to see whether people's minds could nudge the results, and they reportedly found a pattern called the "rebound effect". Jesse Michels tells this several times, from a mentor named John Valentino who he says helped run the lab under its head, Bob Jahn. In other tellings Michels calls it a "skewing effect" with "a ton of corroborated evidence", or stresses how a focused, coherent observer shifts the numbers, which would suggest the mind can touch the physical world.
